source_location: Measuring the Insecurity of Mobile Deep Links of Android / paper, Background and Research Goals
behavior_summary: The original research describes deep link hijacking and demonstrates that unverified schemes can be claimed by another application.

source_location: Android Intents with Chrome / intent URI syntax (package field)
behavior_summary: An intent URI may specify a target package; comparing that declared package with the expected application reveals an identity mismatch.
If an intent cannot launch its target app, a browser fallback URL can direct the user to a different destination.
Deep link parameters and intent extras are attacker controlled and may expose sensitive data or alter app behavior if trusted.

source_location: Auto verification / Digital Asset Links association
behavior_summary: A link cannot be treated as a verified app destination from its text alone; absent association verification leaves the destination uncertain.

source_location: Vulnerability findings / Triggering the app's internal deeplinks
behavior_summary: Microsoft documented a fixed Android deep link validation bypass that could route a crafted link into an unintended WebView destination. The TapLens fixture retains only the idea of comparing declared and actual destinations, not the exploit.
